title: The SSD Pipeline
topic: Higher-order functions: map, filter, reduce, sorted, decorators
briefing: The SSD floor is getting an automated pipeline: machines that take OTHER machines as inputs. In Python, functions can be passed around like any other value. It sounds mind-bending, but it's incredibly powerful. Oh, and security wants every label printer logged. A decorator can do that without touching the printer's code.
hints: map(func, list) runs func on every item and filter(func, list) keeps the items where func is True. Both give back a lazy object, so wrap them in list(). reduce is imported from functools.

sorted(ssds, key=lambda s: s["health"], reverse=True) sorts by health, best first. A decorator is a function that takes a function, defines an inner wrapper that does something extra before calling the original, and returns the wrapper.

gbs = list(map(lambda s: s["gb"], ssds)) / healthy = list(filter(lambda s: s["health"] >= 20, ssds)) / total_gb = reduce(lambda a, b: a + b, gbs) / ranked = sorted(ssds, key=lambda s: s["health"], reverse=True) / def logged(func): def wrapper(*args): print("Running", func.__name__); return func(*args) / return wrapper
bonus: Write a closure: make_checker(limit) that returns a lambda checking s["health"] >= limit. Use it with filter to find drives above 90% health.
